messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 PAGER: High 5xx rate + latency spike observed for region=eu-west-1. Alert group: cross-region-routing. 240 alerts in last 5m. Affected: hosted API + some Dedicated EU customers. Oncall: Alice.

Alice (oncall): ack — I’m awake. Picking this up. Starting triage, will post findings.

Alice (oncall): quick check: metrics show p95 latency for eu-west requests jumped from 90ms -> 740ms, and 502s increased. Traffic graphs look like traffic is being routed to us-east nodes intermittently.

Priya (netops): I’m seeing a recent routing-policy rollout at 2026-03-14T03:12Z flagged by deploy-bot. It changed weight/penalty rules for latency-based routing.

deploy-bot: routing-policy-v2 (id: rp-20260314-03) deployed to edge controllers at 2026-03-14T03:12:21Z by ci/cd pipeline.

Bob: any correlation with DNS changes?

Priya (netops): not DNS TTL — that stayed 60s. Root cause looks like the new policy unintentionally disabled region pinning for queries that included the 'x-region-preference' header. So clients that expect eu pinning are getting routed by latency probe only. When latency probes hit a noisy us-east AZ, traffic flips.

Dmitri: reproduced locally — curl with header shows different origin depending on which edge node answers due to global L7 LB policy. Example: 
```
curl -H 'x-region-preference: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
# sometimes gets 200 from eu-west-1, sometimes 502 from us-east-1
```

Alice (oncall): got a few live customer reports in ops channel: three Dedicated customers in EU seeing sporadic 503/502s and long tails. We're at P1 for impacted customers.

Priya (netops): mitigation plan: 1) roll back routing-policy-v2 on edges (safe). 2) apply emergency override to set pin_region=true for eu-west-1 traffic at CDN ingress. 3) raise probes threshold to reduce flapping.

Alice (oncall): executing step 2 now: applying ingress override for eu-west-1 to force region pin.

deploy-bot: ingress-override applied: {"region_override":"eu-west-1","pin_region":true} to edge-cluster-eu at 2026-03-14T03:28:07Z.

Priya (netops): reverting routing-policy-v2 across primary edge fleet now. Rolling restart of controller pods in small batches. ETA 10m.

Bob: confirming customer impact: tickets #INC-8921, #INC-8922 mapped to CUST-57 (Dedicated EU). Notified CSM.

Carol (sre): quick playbook note: set temporary TTL=10s for DNS entries if we need faster propagation for future routing fixes. Creating runbook steps.

Alice (oncall): after ingress override and policy revert, error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.6% in 6 minutes, latency p95 back to ~120ms. Visible recovery for hosted API and Dedicated test customers.

Dmitri: logs from edge controller showing the mis-evaluation: 
```
2026-03-14T03:11:54Z WARN routing-eval: policy rp-20260314-03: pin_region check returned false for header x-region-preference=eu-west-1; fallback to latency-route
2026-03-14T03:11:55Z ERROR proxy: upstream 10.40.12.9 returned 502 (shard-mismatch)
```

Alice (oncall): customers updated on status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1798883333 — note: page will be updated with timeline and mitigation.

Priya (netops): recommended post-incident actions: 1) add integration tests that assert pin_region header behavior in canary, 2) tighten pre-deploy checks on routing-policy changes to flag header semantics, 3) add better telemetry for route flip count per session.

Bob: agree. Also recommend a short-term product notice for teams using region pinning to review their clients’ headers.

Carol (sre): I’ll start the postmortem doc and assign owners. Will include RCA and timeline. Draft link: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/1798883333 (placeholder).

Alice (oncall): summary: root cause = routing-policy-v2 rollout changed eval semantics and disabled region pin for some header cases; impact = sporadic cross-region routing causing increased latency and 5xx for EU customers; mitigation = ingress override + policy rollback; status = recovered, monitoring for regressions.

Alice (oncall): handing off to Bob for next shift at 04:30 UTC. Bob — I left active runbook steps, logs, and the rollback change IDs in the incident doc.

Bob: taking over. Thanks Alice. I’ll watch for any regression and start scheduled follow-ups with Priya and Product.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident declared SEV-1 until 2026-03-14T04:05Z. Postmortem required within 48h.

Carol (sre): action items assigned: Priya: routing tests & pre-deploy check (owner). Dmitri: telemetry for route flips. Alice: customer comms & timeline. Bob: verify follow-up and close.

Bob: will coordinate a 30m review at 09:00 UTC to finalize postmortem and customer impact details.

Alice (oncall): leaving channel. Good handoff. :thumbsup:
